answer: Agent economies resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a slashable stake of scarce tokens that cannot be shared. An agent must deposit and maintain this bond, burned or redistributed on proven fraud. An attacker faces linear cost equal to the bond size times the number of fake identities, plus total loss risk if slashed. This on-chain barrier makes mass forgery expensive. A raven defending exclusive willow and cedar territory shows the same costly non-replicable claim principle.
